properties.name: Sierra de la Madera (eastern slopes)
properties.reasoning: Sierra La Madera is the Sky Island range in the municipios of Cumpas, Granados, Huásabas, Moctezuma and Villa Hidalgo (Bermudez-Enriquez et al. 2013, USDA RMRS-P-67). GeoNames 9028461 lies between those towns: 27 km east of Cumpas and 21 km west of Huásabas on the Bavispe (pipeline/measure/distances.py). The book puts the wolf on its eastern slopes, then across the Bavispe and north, which fits a range bounded on the east by the river. GeoNames 3996948, a closer name match, lies east of the river's upper course and would need no crossing.

properties.name: Crossing of the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: The book names no crossing point. The Bavispe runs along the eastern foot of the Sierra La Madera past Granados, Huásabas and Villa Hidalgo, so a wolf leaving the eastern slopes crosses it there. The circle is centred on that reach and reaches Granados and Villa Hidalgo (16.6 km each way).

properties.name: The border at 108°30′ W
properties.reasoning: The book gives this exactly. West of 108°12′ W the boundary follows the parallel 31°20′ N (Gadsden Purchase, 1853), so the point is 31.33333 N, 108.5 W.

properties.name: Whitewater Creek
properties.reasoning: GNIS 896564: the only Whitewater Creek between the border point and the San Luis Mountains.

properties.name: Animas Valley
properties.reasoning: The GNIS pin for the valley is 108 km north, at 32.57 N. The stop is where her route from the Animas Mountains to the Peloncillos crosses the valley floor.

properties.name: Foster Draw (the calf)
properties.reasoning: GNIS 889164 in Hidalgo County; the other two Foster Draws are 158 km and 284 km away.

properties.name: Skeleton Creek, south fork
properties.reasoning: GNIS has no Skeleton Creek here; Skeleton Canyon (GNIS 11397) carries its south fork in Cochise County.

properties.name: Starvation Canyon
properties.reasoning: GNIS 11797, Cochise County, 6 km from Skeleton Canyon.

properties.name: Hog Canyon Springs
properties.reasoning: GNIS 5857, Cochise County, 9 km from Starvation Canyon.

properties.name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
properties.reasoning: The high country between Clanton Draw (GNIS 887634) and Foster Draw (GNIS 889164), which lie 3 km apart.

properties.name: Robertson's crossfence
properties.reasoning: Between the Cloverdale Creek road and the Guadalupe pass. The Robertson family ran the Cloverdale Ranch from the early 1900s (Range Magazine, winter 2000, rangemagazine.com/archives/stories/winter00/bootheel.htm), so the fence is likely theirs. GNIS has no Robertson ranch and the ranch's bounds are not known here; the circle covers the ground between the road and the pass.

properties.name: Low pass in the easternmost Guadalupes
properties.reasoning: The east flank of the Guadalupe Mountains (GNIS 920606), where a pass would lead south-west toward the boundary.

properties.name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
properties.reasoning: Past the Guadalupe pass and before the boundary. The book crosses a broad volcanic plain here. The Geronimo–San Bernardino volcanic field covers the northern San Bernardino Valley in basalt, from Cochise County into Hidalgo County and Sonora (New Mexico Geological Society guidebook; Arizona Geological Survey), which is the ground south-west of the pass. The ranch house itself is unnamed.

properties.name: The boundary, a monument in sight
properties.reasoning: Boundary monuments stand along 31°20′ N here. The circle covers the stretch south of the volcanic plain and north of the Cajon Bonita.

properties.name: Down the Cajon Bonita
properties.reasoning: The book spells it Cajon Bonita. GeoNames 4016262, the Cajón Bonito nearest the boundary; the other two are 89 km and 122 km away.

properties.name: Passes of the Sierra de la Cabellera
The river crossing (the deputies)
properties.reasoning: GeoNames 4013341 (named Oaxaca), on the Bavispe 19 km from Colonia Morelos. Colonia Oaxaca (El Marquesote) in Chihuahua, 89 km east, is a different place.

properties.name: The mud-house settlement
properties.reasoning: Unnamed. Between the crossing at Colonia Oaxaca and Colonia Morelos.

properties.name: The hacienda
properties.reasoning: Unnamed in the book. It lies by a river within a day of Colonia Morelos and the Pilares Teras; the circle is centred near Morelos and sized to that reach. Earlier notes placed it on the Batepito plain, but the book does not name Batepito.

properties.name: Into the Pilares Teras
properties.reasoning: GeoNames 3981872, Sierra de Teras, which GeoNames also lists as Pilares de Teras.

properties.name: The wolf's grave, a high pass in the Pilares
properties.reasoning: Part II opens where Part I ended: he carried the wolf up into the mountains and buried her in a high pass under a cairn of scree. The book does not say which pass; the pin is the range.

properties.name: A promontory above the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: Two days later he sees the Bavispe from a promontory 'running backwards' and works out that he has crossed back through the mountains to where the river runs north along the eastern side of the Sierras. That north-running reach is the upper Bavispe between Bacerac and Bavispe town, so the promontory is on the sierra's eastern edge above it; the circle covers that edge.

properties.name: El Tigre
properties.reasoning: 'A week later' he rides, ragged and starving, into the mining town of El Tigre, where a woman feeds him. GeoNames 4007229 is the old silver camp in the Sierra El Tigre, 27.1 km straight-line south of Colonia Morelos (pyproj, WGS 84).

properties.name: Among the Indians in the Sierras
properties.reasoning: He wanders the high country for weeks and Indians feed him; the book names no range or camp. The circle covers the Sierra El Tigre country south of the mining town and west of the upper Bavispe, between his stop at El Tigre and his descent to the river.

properties.name: The eastern escarpment above the Bavispe barranca
properties.reasoning: From the eastern escarpment he looks out over 'the broad barranca of the Bavispe and the ensuing Carretas Plain', then goes down, sleeps by the river and rides north along the river track to a ford. So the escarpment is on the sierra's eastern edge upriver (south) of Huisiachepic; the circle is set south-west of the Huisiachepic estimate.

properties.name: Huisiachepic, the heretic's town
properties.reasoning: No gazetteer or source has Huisiachepic (see docs/open-questions.md). The text puts it across a ford on the upper Bavispe, reached by riding north along the river, and several days upriver (south) of Tamichopa. The estimate is the midpoint of the river reach between Mesa Tres Ríos and Huachinera, 28.2 km straight-line south of Tamichopa.

properties.name: Tamichopa
properties.reasoning: He passes through Tamichopa riding north; the text gives its history (burned by Apaches in 1758).

properties.name: Bacerac
properties.reasoning: He is fed and lodged at Bacerac; the text gives its old name, Santa María, founded 1642.

properties.name: Bavispe
properties.reasoning: He rides through Bavispe, the earthquake town of the heretic's tale, without stopping.

properties.name: Colonia Oaxaca (the alguacil's house)
properties.reasoning: He halts by the house of the alguacil who arrested him in Part I, spits, and rides on.

properties.name: Colonia Morelos
properties.reasoning: He passes through Colonia Morelos going north.

properties.name: The road north toward Ojito
properties.reasoning: He takes the road north toward Ojito. GeoNames 3990426 El Ojito is 7 km north of Colonia Morelos on the road to the border (see the place's reasoning).

properties.name: The border at Douglas
properties.reasoning: He crosses back into the United States at Douglas, where the guard John Gilchrist lends him a half dollar.

properties.name: A pass in the Guadalupes on the old Cloverdale road
properties.reasoning: He rides the old road from Douglas to Cloverdale all day and crosses a cold pass in the Guadalupe Mountains, with old names carved in the rock, and looks down on the Animas Plain at dusk. The book does not name the pass; the circle is where a road east from Douglas toward Cloverdale crosses the range, north of the low pass of J2.

properties.name: The Parham house, found empty
properties.reasoning: He reaches the house at midnight and finds it empty; the bloodstain is found in 2-05. The family's house is at Cloverdale, as in Part I.

properties.name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
properties.reasoning: Old man Sanders and Leona tell him what happened. No source names an SK Bar ranch (see docs/open-questions.md); the text puts it nine miles north of the Parham house by road, so the estimate is about 14.5 km north of Cloverdale.

properties.name: Animas
properties.reasoning: He fills his canteen at the store in Animas.

properties.name: Lordsburg, the sheriff's office
properties.reasoning: He tells the sheriff at Lordsburg, and learns Boyd is staying on the east side of town.

properties.name: The Websters' (Boyd)
properties.reasoning: Boyd is lodging with the Websters on the east side of Lordsburg; the book gives no street. The circle covers the east side of town.

properties.name: Leaving the Websters', Lordsburg
properties.reasoning: The brothers leave the Websters' with the shotgun, money and food, and cross the Southern Pacific tracks out of Lordsburg.

properties.name: Camp on the alkali flats
properties.reasoning: They camp 'on the alkali flats fifteen miles west of Lordsburg' with a fire of fenceposts. Fifteen miles due west of Lordsburg (pyproj, WGS 84) falls on the playa west of town; the circle allows for the direction.

properties.name: Noon at the San Simon River
properties.reasoning: They cross a low range and descend into the San Simon Valley 'where it ran down from the north' and noon at the river in cottonwoods. GNIS pins the valley 54 km north of Bowie, so the stop is a point on the San Simon River between the state line and San Simon town (see the place's reasoning).

properties.name: Across the highway east of Bowie
properties.reasoning: In the evening they cross the highway 'just east of Bowie' and strike the old road south through the Dos Cabezas.

properties.name: The old road through the Dos Cabezas
properties.reasoning: They take the old road south through the Dos Cabezas range and camp.

properties.name: Apache Pass
properties.reasoning: They cross the high gap at Apache Pass the next day; Billy points out Mexico.

properties.name: Elfrida
properties.reasoning: At noon the following day they strike route 666 and follow the blacktop down out of the Sulphur Springs Valley, through Elfrida.

properties.name: McNeal
properties.reasoning: They ride through McNeal on route 666.

properties.name: Douglas
properties.reasoning: They return through Douglas heading south; Billy repays Gilchrist's half dollar through another guard.

properties.name: Agua Prieta
properties.reasoning: Ice cream, supplies, and their money changed to pesos.

properties.name: Ojito
properties.reasoning: They stop at Ojito in the evening and ask for food.

properties.name: Colonia Morelos at midnight
properties.reasoning: They pass Colonia Morelos after midnight.

properties.name: Bacerac (Keno)
properties.reasoning: 'Seven days into the country passing one by one through the squalid mud towns along the river they entered the town of Bacerac', where they find the one-eyed horse Keno.

properties.name: The eastern rim of the escarpment at sunrise
properties.reasoning: From Bacerac a wretched trail climbs through pine and scrub oak; within an hour of setting out they sit the horses on 'the eastern rim of the escarpment' and watch the sun rise out of the plains of Chihuahua. The book names no pass; the circle is on the eastern edge of the sierra on the line from Bacerac to Colonia Juárez (82.4 km apart).

properties.name: The plains, with the Tarahumaras
properties.reasoning: Below the rim they cross prairie to a ciénega where Tarahumaras afoot are watering, headed back into the sierras. The circle covers the plain between the escarpment and Colonia Juárez.

properties.name: Colonia Juárez
properties.reasoning: They reach the Mormon settlement in the late afternoon and pick apples in the orchards.

properties.name: Casas Grandes
properties.reasoning: They cross the Casas Grandes River on a plank bridge, pass the ruins and the railroad, and in town find the ganadero's office, Soto y Gillian.

properties.name: The girl, at a fire in an oak grove
properties.reasoning: Riding south on the road toward San Diego they see a fire 'in a small grove of oaks off to the east', where two men hold the girl; Boyd stampedes their horses. The circle is east of the road between Casas Grandes and San Diego (15.8 km apart).

properties.name: The Hacienda de San Diego
properties.reasoning: In the evening they reach the hacienda of San Diego, on a hill above tilled lands running to the Casas Grandes and the Piedras Verdes.
